ayahs.textEnglishTranslation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
[All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds -

ayahs.textUthmani: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
ayahs.textEnglishTranslation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

ayahs.textUthmani: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ
ayahs.textEnglishTranslation: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.

tafsirSources.bookTitleArabic: جامع البيان عن تأويل آي القرآن
tafsirSources.author: Al-Tabari (الطبري)

interpretiveClaims.opinionEnglish: The Basmalah is a full, independent verse at the start of Al-Fatiha according to the Shafi'i legal school, Imam Ahmad in one prominent narration, and the reciters of Mecca and Kufa. Ibn Kathir confirms that reciting it (aloud or silently) is authentically supported by narrations from the Companions.
interpretiveClaims.opinionArabic: البسملة آية مستقلة في أول سورة الفاتحة عند الشافعي وأحمد في رواية وقراء مكة والكوفة، وثبت الجهر والإسرار بها عن جماعة من الصحابة.
interpretiveClaims.evidenceEnglish: Transmissions in Sunan al-Daraqutni and canonical Kufan scriptural numbering counting it as verse 1.

interpretiveClaims.opinionEnglish: The Basmalah is not a verse of Al-Fatiha, nor is it a verse of any chapter in the Quran except inside Surah An-Naml (27:30). According to Imam Malik and the Madinan school, it was revealed for blessing and delimiting chapters, not as a counted ayah.
interpretiveClaims.opinionArabic: ليست البسملة آية من الفاتحة ولا من غيرها من السور إلا في سورة النمل. وهو المعتمد في مذهب الإمام مالك وأهل المدينة، ونزلت للتبرك والفصل بين السور.
interpretiveClaims.evidenceEnglish: The unbroken communal practice of Medina (Amal Ahl al-Madinah) and the authentic hadith of Aisha (RA) confirming the Prophet initiated recitation directly with 'Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-Alamin'.

interpretiveClaims.opinionEnglish: Al-Asr signifies the totality of time, the passage of day and night (Ad-Dahr). Allah swears by time because human endeavor, triumph, and ruin are all manifested within its temporal continuum.
interpretiveClaims.opinionArabic: المراد بالعصر الدهر ومرور الليل والنهار، أقسم الله به لأن فيه معتبرًا بمرور الآجال وانقضاء الأعمار وتبدل الأحوال.
interpretiveClaims.evidenceEnglish: Classical Arabic linguistics and narrations from Ibn Abbas confirming time as the overarching vessel of human accountability.

interpretiveClaims.opinionEnglish: While acknowledging the general interpretation of time, Ibn Kathir highlights an authoritative complementary interpretation that 'Al-Asr' refers specifically to the late afternoon prayer (Salat al-Asr / Al-Salat al-Wusta), celebrated for its exceptional sanctity.
interpretiveClaims.opinionArabic: مع شمول العصر لعموم الدهر، روي عن طائفة من السلف تخصيصه بصلاة العصر لفضلها وشرفها وعظيم منزلتها.
interpretiveClaims.evidenceEnglish: Prophetic warnings concerning the forfeiture of one's entire household and property upon missing the Asr prayer.

interpretiveClaims.opinionEnglish: Unanimous scholarly consensus holds that 'Al-Hayy' establishes the Ever-Living possessing eternal life without inception or cessation, while 'Al-Qayyum' denotes the Self-Sufficient who autonomously sustains all of creation.
interpretiveClaims.opinionArabic: إجماع المفسرين قاطبة على أن الحي هو الباقي الذي لا يموت ولا بداءة لحياته ولا نهاية، والقيوم هو القائم بنفسه القيم على حفظ خلقه وتدبير أمورهم.
interpretiveClaims.evidenceEnglish: Universal consensus across narrative and linguistic traditions and hadiths linking these two names with the Supreme Name (Al-Ism al-A'zam).
